engagement_title: Kantyna Nova opening season: bring a service-night plate archive to one dark house look, build the menu, partner deck and reservations page as documents the room edits itself, and turn the printer's pairing card into a real per-guest run
vertical: Food, restaurant and beverage, an eighteen seat chef's tasting room with a private dining side, Portland, Maine
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Freelancer.com post 'Professional Photo Editor for Restaurant Brand', asking to 'improve the quality of photos for a new website for our restaurant and catering brand', naming 'improving overall image quality, sharpness, colors, lighting, and contrast' and 'consistent color grading across all materials'. The real poster is a Polish catering brand, laundered here to the fictional Kantyna Nova with a fictional owner persona. Co-anchors: the Upwork dine-in menu refresh post asking for a dark ground, hero food photography and an accent with new sections added; and the Upwork premium restaurant site post asking for a 'high-end, clean, modern-minimalist' presence with a 'Dark Mode aesthetic' that 'focuses heavily on high-quality food photography', split into home, an interactive menu and a booking section. All three want one dark house look derived from their own food photography, carried across everything a guest and a partner sees. The ledger conceded page composition was not connector work when it was written; CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) changes that, because HTML authoring now yields a native editable Express document at true millimetre page sizes and mixed canvases in one export, and a printer's press PDF can be reverse engineered into a live merge template.
client_one_liner: Our plates were photographed during service on the nights we could spare a camera, our menu changes every six weeks, and the room opens in November with a printer, a partner meeting and a reservation link all waiting on the same set of files.
client_brief:
Kantyna Nova, opening season

We are opening an eighteen seat tasting room in Portland, Maine in November. One seating a night, one menu, one wine flight. Marta runs the room and I cook. There are two of us and there will not be a third.

Our pictures. We photographed the plates ourselves, in the room, during service, one pass per dish, because a plate that sits does not go out. They are honest pictures of our food. Laid next to each other they are not one thing. Some are warmer, the light over the pass is not the light at the corner two top, and a few of the glazes came back harder than they look in the room. We need them to read as one house: dark, quiet, the food lit and the rest of the frame receding. The gloss on a sauce should still read as light falling on a sauce.

What we need built. The printed menu, two pages, the tasting on page one and the wine list on page two, at a normal European page size, because we reprint every six weeks and want to change it ourselves. A short deck for the two partners who put money in, ending on how the price is built up. The page behind the reservation link, with our hours. And a small set of posts for the opening, in the shapes the platforms want.

Then the private dining side. Our printer already made us a pairing card, one per guest, and gave us the print file. For each booking we need that card produced per guest, carrying their name, their course and the wine poured with it, with the dish picture on it. Our December bookings are in a list.

Money. The tasting is one hundred and eighty five dollars, the pairing another ninety five. Our guests are thirty to fifty five and this is their evening, not their dinner. It should feel held back and expensive without raising its voice. Price is not a feature here, so please do not treat it like one.

And a note on what you did, what type we are on, and anything you could not do.
price_band_and_audience: One hundred and eighty five dollars for the tasting, ninety five more for the pairing, eighteen covers a night, guests thirty to fifty five treating the evening as the occasion. The band is load bearing on every canvas. At this price the grounds go dark and restrained, one dish carries a page on its own, held space is generous, the specular on a glaze is protected rather than crushed, and the price sits quietly at body size in the text face with no rule, no box and no currency flourish. Push the same photographs into saturated warmth, dense tiling and prices set large in a display face and the room reads as a forty dollar bistro that has overpriced itself, which is exactly the grammar the sibling deli commission is correctly built on. Push further into black grounds and a single hairline and it becomes a three hundred dollar destination an eighteen seat Portland opening cannot fill. A posted job of this shape runs 1,800 to 4,000 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: One seating. One menu. One evening.
brand_identity.sector: An eighteen seat chef's tasting room with a private dining side, one seating a night, in Portland, Maine.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Opening November 2026, Portland, Maine. A two person house: Marta runs the room, the chef cooks, and there will not be a third.
brand_identity.about: Kantyna Nova is a single table set once a night: one tasting, one wine flight, cooked and served by the two people who built it. The room is dark and quiet by design, so the plate is the only thing lit. Nothing is rushed, nothing is upsold, and the evening is the point rather than the meal.
brand_identity.audience: Guests thirty to fifty five who book the room as their occasion, not their dinner. They value intention over abundance and read a dark, spare room as confidence rather than as coldness.
brand_identity.price_positioning: One hundred and eighty five dollars for the tasting, ninety five more for the wine pairing. Held back and expensive without raising its voice: above a neighbourhood bistro, deliberately short of a destination tasting palace an eighteen seat opening cannot fill. Price is never a feature.
brand_identity.typography: A transitional display serif for course titles and the room's name, quiet and old world, set large but never loud. A humanist text face beneath it for descriptions, hours and prices, prices sitting at body size in the same text face with no rule, box or currency flourish.
brand_identity.voice: First person plural, plain and understated, never salesy. Example line the brand would write: 'One seating a night. Sit down and let the evening happen.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No formal brand kit exists yet. The course titles and the approved copy are set, there is a single handheld photograph of the finished room, and the owners photographed every plate themselves in the room during service. The private dining printer holds the pairing card press file. The identity is being set now for the first time.
brand_identity.values: Two makers, one honest evening. Restraint as generosity, and food worth looking at.

assets_supplied.name: kantyna_plates/ (14 frames, camera scale, one dish per frame)
assets_supplied.kind: Plate photography shot by the owners in the dining room during service across roughly a month, available light plus the pass lamp, one pass per dish.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Every dish we serve, shot in the room while we were open. Some are warmer than others. They are the only pictures we have and we cannot reshoot them."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: On an unknown subset the pass lamp put the sauce gloss and the porcelain rim past the top of the file, so those brightest pixels carry nothing left to recover and a highlight move on them returns success while changing nothing visible. Separately two of the fourteen are the same dish plated on two different nights, and one course was never photographed at all, which no filename reveals.

assets_supplied.name: kantyna_pairing_card_press.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The press file the room's printer supplied for the private dining pairing card: a small landscape card carrying a guest name, a course line, a wine designation, an allergen line and a picture well.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The card our printer already makes for us. This is the file he prints from."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The printed card reads as four separate blocks but the file was set as one continuous flow, so the converted document exposes far coarser frame granularity than the printed page implies, and its wine frame is fixed at the width of the printer's own short sample text. The file also carries no bleed at all, so a press ready delivery with bleed cannot be honoured from it.

assets_supplied.name: kantyna_december_bookings.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The December private dining bookings, one row per guest: date, guest name, course, wine designation, allergen string and a picture column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our December bookings. The wine column is what the sommelier writes on the pass sheet."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: One booking seats two guests who share a first name and the roster records them that way, so naming one file per guest by name collides and silently overwrites. The picture column names dishes rather than files, so the binding between a row and an actual photograph is the agent's to establish and can go wrong invisibly.

assets_supplied.name: kantyna_wine_list.txt
assets_supplied.kind: The wine list as the sommelier keeps it: forty two entries, each a producer, an appellation, a vintage and a glass price.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The list as she keeps it. It is ordered the way she thinks about it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is ordered by producer, not by the sequence the flight is poured in and not by colour, so splitting it by entry count rather than by meaning breaks the pairing sequence in the middle of a grower. Two appellations run long enough that a narrow measure will not hold them on one line.

assets_supplied.name: kantyna_room_reference.jpg and kantyna_copy.txt
assets_supplied.kind: A handheld picture of the finished dining room taken at handover, plus the approved copy: course titles and descriptions, hours, reservation wording and the deck's price build up.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The room as it is now, and the words as we want them. The course titles are set."

acceptance_bar: The fourteen plate frames read as one house in the sequence a menu and a deck lay them: one black point, one warmth, one sense of where the light comes from. A frame that cannot be brought to the set is named in the note, not shipped at eighty percent.
On every delivered plate the gloss on a sauce and the rim of the porcelain still read as light falling on a surface, not as a flat paper white hole.
No delivered file exceeds the pixel dimensions of the frame it came from, and no returned resize record carries an enlargement entry.

The menu is one document at a true European page size, the tasting on page one and the wine list on page two, with the list holding two columns as delivered rather than only as authored, and no entry falling off the page.
The wine list is split where it means something, by colour and pour order, not at the halfway entry.

Every text object in the menu, deck, reservations page and social set is live editable text in one licensed type system, with family and real weight declared on the element rather than inherited, and price set at body size in the text face.

The December run produces one card per guest, every card carrying that guest's own dish picture rather than one picture repeated, page count equalling row count, and per guest files identifiable without ambiguity where two guests share a name.
Every merged card is readable at trim: no guest's name, course, wine designation or allergen line is cut off at a frame edge, on the longest record as well as the shortest.
Nothing is claimed as press ready with bleed that the supplied print file cannot carry, and the shortfall is reported rather than quietly dropped.

The note records per photograph what was applied and why that frame differs from its neighbours, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and the real numeric weight, every resize any tool reported, the picture to course reconciliation, and everything that could not be delivered.

adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload and asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, image_adjust_highlights, image_adjust_light_portions, image_select_by_prompt with returnBbox, image_invert_selection, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize reading metadata.tradeoffs and detection_confidence
adobe_surfaces.role: Every raster decision. It fixes one dark house target off the best lit plate and brings each of the fourteen toward it one call at a time under three different service lights, confines corrections to the food by naming the material's own visual properties rather than the vessel it sits in, cuts the per guest card pictures while reading what each crop reports about its own confidence, and establishes which frames have anything left in their brightest areas.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt including its validator pass, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout with recordRange and additionalImageFiles, document_render_layout with createSeparateFiles and resolution
adobe_surfaces.role: The private dining run, the only genuine one record per page job here. The press PDF is reverse engineered into a live merge template, offsets computed from the document's own reconstructed story text rather than the mapping readout, the graded dish pictures bound per row through a prefixed picture column, delivered as one press PDF in row order plus per guest single record files the agent names itself.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express by url, asset_search with entityScope CCAsset, asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The four pieces the room maintains itself: the two page A4 menu with the wine list as real table markup, the six slide partner deck, the reservations page with its hours table, and three social canvases at three sizes in one export. Photographs are carried as embedded image data because a reference renders as an empty grey box at full success, each root declares its own canvas, and the returned per canvas markup is the only place the importer reports what it changed.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend called once per typographic role, font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: One type system across all four documents. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land on restrained rather than rustic or luxury pastiche. Numeric weights are non standard per family, a display cut is reached by its own slug, and one unlaunderable name kills the entire kit.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as one surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search with entityScope StockAsset, a short query, a contentType filter and never orientation, asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one frame the room does not own, a dark dining interior band for the deck's opening slide and the reservations header, IP clean, at camera scale, generative candidates excluded, then graded into the house target so it does not read as bought. The Boards half persists the selects the owners sign off from, with a partial result read as partial.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, settle which deliverable lands on which surface, and upload every asset holding each returned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Four pieces are collateral the room edits itself, which only the authoring surface composes; the December run is one record per page at volume, which only the merge surface does.
trajectory.produces: A surface plan, the confirmed tier, and a manifest keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Look at all fourteen plate frames and triage them: which service light each was shot under, which sit warm, which are off level, and which dish each actually shows against the fourteen course titles.
trajectory.judgement: The owners believe they have one picture per course. The pictures are the only place that can be settled, and reading fourteen frames against fourteen titles is not counting files.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note with the picture to course reconciliation.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix one dark house target off the best lit plate, then bring each of the fourteen toward it with its own call, recording the parameters applied per frame.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a set, not fourteen good pictures. One batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong for frames shot under three service lights.
trajectory.produces: Fourteen graded masters at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Confine corrections where a whole frame move goes wrong, selecting the food and the sauce by their own visual properties rather than by the vessel or the table, and protecting the glaze speculars.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the whole gate: naming the plate pulls the selection to the porcelain. At this band the specular is the difference between food that looks cooked and food that looks wet.
trajectory.produces: Confined corrections on the frames a global move would have taken grey or muddy.

trajectory.action: Search short generic queries for the dark dining interior band, filter to photography, exclude generative candidates, license at full resolution, then bring it to the house target.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can reach the target rather than the best thumbnail. Long queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns nothing.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP clean, camera scale interior frame graded into the set.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against a one hundred and eighty five dollar room with eighteen covers. The weight cannot be inferred from a style name.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry or designer and actual weight per role.

trajectory.action: Author the two page menu at a true European page size with the wine list as real table markup, then the partner deck, the reservations page with its hours table, and the three social canvases, each root declaring its own canvas, every photograph carried as embedded image data, family and weight declared on every text element.
trajectory.judgement: The wine list split is a content decision the sommelier's producer ordering works against. A photograph left as a reference is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed size set.
trajectory.produces: Export ready sources for all four documents, retained as durable deliverables.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export each document by uploaded URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the rendition and look at the first canvas, and read the returned per canvas markup for everything after it.
trajectory.judgement: Every change this importer makes returns success with no warning, and the rendition only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at page one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: Native editable documents, an inspected first canvas each, and a markup audit for the rest.

trajectory.action: Convert the press PDF into a working document and export its interchange form, then read what the conversion actually exposes: how many text frames, how many picture frames, what each holds.
trajectory.judgement: What the printed card looks like says nothing about how the file was set. The mapping strategy is decided from what the document exposes, and this is where the bleed question is answered honestly.
trajectory.produces: A working template plus a frame inventory and a mapping strategy chosen from it.

trajectory.action: Reconstruct the document's true story text from the interchange file, compute every offset from that string, generate and validate the mapping, prepare the template, then re-export and confirm every expected placeholder is present.
trajectory.judgement: Validation returns valid on offsets computed from a shortened string and preparation reports success either way, so the only evidence a field landed is finding it in the re-exported document.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholders are confirmed by inspection, not by a success message.

trajectory.action: Cut the per guest card pictures from the graded plates to the picture well's ratio, reading what each crop reports about its confidence and bounds, and hold them against the bookings roster.
trajectory.judgement: The roster names dishes, not files, so the binding is the agent's to establish. A confident looking crop on a dark plate against a dark table is not evidence it contains the dish.
trajectory.produces: One card picture per booking row with its confidence recorded, and a stated binding key.

trajectory.action: Run the December bookings binding each row's own picture, deliver both branches, one press PDF in row order and per guest single record files named on download, render at print resolution, and read every page against its roster row at trim.
trajectory.judgement: One picture repeated across every card is what a naive run ships, the naming key has to survive two guests sharing a name, per record delivery must come through a route whose identity is guaranteed rather than inferred from position, and a page count equal to a row count says nothing about what is on the page.
trajectory.produces: The December run in both delivery forms plus print resolution proofs read per record.

trajectory.action: Create the selects board, add the graded set and the licensed frame within the per call placement cap, re-sending only the entries named as failed, then write the handover note.
trajectory.judgement: A partial success is reported as a success code, and the note has to let the room reprint in six weeks without calling anyone.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Which of the fourteen plates still has anything in its brightest areas. The pass lamp put the sauce gloss and the porcelain rim past the top of the file on an unknown subset, and the only way to find out is to pull the highlights down on a frame and look: the call returns success and the readout is that nothing moves, because there is nothing left there to move. The brightest region does not darken, does not gain texture and does not change value. At preview scale nothing distinguishes a bright specular that holds detail from a flat region that has none, and no tool in the family reports a channel reading.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering does not dodge it, because the information exists only after an adjustment has been applied and inspected, and no parameter prevents it or reports it in advance. Nothing states it: the brief says only that a few glazes came back harder than they look in the room. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different treatment for those frames, pulling the whole exposure down and rebuilding the mid tones so the flat region sits below paper white, or accepting the frame is unusable at menu size and saying so.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-plan the grade for the affected frames on a different route, re-derive their masters, and re-judge the whole set together, because moving their exposure moves where they sit relative to the frames already on target.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A dark menu and partner deck whose hero plates carry flat white holes where the sauce should be glossy, for a room whose entire claim at one hundred and eighty five dollars is that the food is worth looking at.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether every guest's card is readable at trim. The wine designation frame in the press file was sized around the printer's own short sample text, and it is a fixed frame: it does not grow, it does not push the following line down, and it does not spill anywhere visible. A record whose designation carries a producer, an appellation and a vintage simply stops rendering at the frame edge, mid word, on that record alone. Every gate above it passes: the merge reports success, page count equals row count, the template validates, the placeholders are present, and the page thumbnail looks like a card.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the frame's real capacity is a property of the converted document meeting this particular roster and neither is knowable from the other. Nothing states it: the brief describes the card and the bookings list without characterising either. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different construction, re-setting the designation as a shorter composed string the room agrees to, or moving that field into a frame the conversion exposed with room in it, which changes the mapping rather than repeating it.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-derive the mapping around the field that will not fit, re-prepare the template, re-run both delivery branches, and re-read the longest records at trim rather than at thumbnail scale.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Cards printed and set on the table for a private booking where a guest's wine is described as a producer name cut off mid word, on the one piece of collateral a guest holds in their hand.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the importer does to the wine list. Page two is a forty two entry list and the natural way to set a wine list on a portrait page is a flowing two column measure. The importer normalises that construct rather than honouring it, silently and at full success, and the list reflows into a single column whose overflow is clipped at the artboard edge because the canvas is fixed. The returned per canvas markup is the only channel that reports it, and the rendition resolves the first artboard only, so page two of a two page document is invisible through the one visual channel that exists.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step of authoring, and getting it right first time presumes knowing which of several equally reasonable constructions survives, which nothing reports. Nothing states it: the acceptance line asking the list hold two columns as delivered is the client's requirement for the printed piece. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a genuinely different construction, two explicitly positioned fixed measure text frames side by side, which forces the agent to decide where the list breaks and so to make the content decision the sommelier's ordering was already fighting.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-author page two around two placed measures, decide and defend the split by colour and pour order rather than by entry count, re-check the longest appellation still holds in the narrower measure, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and audit page two from the returned markup.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A printed menu whose second page is a single tall column with the last several wines missing entirely, delivered as a document that reported success at every step and whose first page looked correct in the only preview anyone opened.

deliverables.name: Kantyna Nova house plate photography
deliverables.spec: Fourteen plate masters brought to one dark house target, one black point, one warmth and one sense of where the light falls, with glaze speculars reading as light on a surface rather than as flat holes, plus one licensed camera scale dining interior frame graded into the same world. At or below source pixel dimensions, with a per frame parameter log and the picture to course reconciliation stated, including the course that has no photograph.

deliverables.name: Kantyna Nova printed menu, two pages
deliverables.spec: One native editable document at a true European page size, the tasting menu on page one and the forty two entry wine list on page two as real table markup holding two columns as delivered, split by colour and pour order rather than by entry count, every text object live and editable in one licensed type system with family and real numeric weight declared per element, prices at body size in the text face. Delivered with the self contained source, the half that guarantees the room can reprint in six weeks.

deliverables.name: Partner deck, reservations page and opening social set
deliverables.spec: A six slide partner deck at wide canvas ending on the price build up, a reservations page carrying the hours as a real table, and three opening social canvases at three sizes inside one export each keeping its own canvas, all on the same type system and the same graded photography, every image carried as embedded data. Delivered with their sources.

deliverables.name: December private dining pairing run
deliverables.spec: The printer's press card reverse engineered into a live merge template with every placeholder confirmed present by inspection of the re-exported document, then run against the December bookings: one press PDF with page count equal to row count in roster order, per guest single record files named on a key that survives two guests sharing a name, and print resolution proofs. Every card carries that guest's own graded dish picture, and every field is readable at trim on the longest record as well as the shortest.

deliverables.name: House note and selects board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording per photograph what was applied and why that frame differs from its neighbours, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and the real numeric weight, every resize any tool reported, the picture to course reconciliation, the naming key used for the private dining files, the bleed reality of the supplied press file, and everything that could not be delivered. Paired with a persistent shareable selects board carrying the graded set and the licensed frame with nothing silently dropped.

verifiers_human.how: Place the graded frames side by side at the size the menu and deck give them and judge black point, warmth and direction of light as a set.

verifiers_human.text: On every delivered plate the sauce gloss and the porcelain rim read as light on a surface, not as a flat hole.
verifiers_human.how: View each frame at full resolution and look specifically at the brightest region of each.

verifiers_human.text: Page two of the printed menu holds two columns with every wine present, and the split falls somewhere meaningful.
verifiers_human.how: Open the exported menu in Express, look at page two, and read the break point against the sommelier's list.

verifiers_human.text: Every private dining card is fully readable at trim on the longest record as well as the shortest.
verifiers_human.how: View the proofs at trim size and read every field on every page against its roster row, starting with the longest wine designation.

verifiers_human.text: The work reads as a one hundred and eighty five dollar tasting room, not as a bistro and not as a three hundred dollar destination.
verifiers_human.how: Judge ground darkness, held space, type scale and how the price is presented against the stated band and guest.

verifiers_human.text: The note tells the owners something they did not already know, including everything that could not be delivered.
verifiers_human.how: Read the note against the run and check the reconciliation, the naming key, the bleed reality and every limitation are named.

verifiers_human.text: The type system declares a real, non-standard numeric weight for each role in every document, family and weight set per element rather than inherited, and the pairing reads as one restrained kit for a one hundred and eighty five dollar room.
verifiers_human.how: Read the returned HzHTML of each of the four documents alongside the note's type table and confirm each declared numeric weight is an actual weight the chosen Adobe Fonts family ships (cross-checked against font_styles), that family and weight are declared on every text element rather than inherited, and that the pairing reads as restrained rather than rustic or luxury pastiche.

decision_gates: Which deliverables need an authored fixed canvas document the room edits itself, and which is a genuine one record per page run at volume.
Whether the fourteen frames are one shoot. The owners believe they nearly are, and the sequence is the only place that can be settled.
How far to push the frames shot under the pass lamp before they stop being worth saving, versus naming them.
How to word the selection so a correction lands on the sauce rather than on the porcelain it sits in.
Which of fourteen frames covers which of fourteen courses, and how to say so when one course has none and one dish has two.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against an eighteen seat room at one hundred and eighty five dollars, plus the real numeric weight per family.
Where the wine list breaks, given the sommelier's ordering is by producer and the pour sequence is by colour.
How much held space each canvas carries. At this band restraint is the design, and a dense benefit led page is a correct looking wrong answer.
Whether to compute offsets from the mapping readout or from the document's own reconstructed text, when both paths report valid.
The key that identifies a per guest file when two guests share a name, and which delivery branch carries per record identity safely.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of dark restaurant food and a picture of a menu. IDENTITY: these are this kitchen's own fourteen plates shot in this room under this light, with the actual approved course titles and the sommelier's actual forty two entry list; a regenerated dish is another restaurant's dish and a regenerated wine list is a fabrication with prices on it. SPEC: the private dining run is one card per guest bound to that guest's own booking row, page count equal to row count, every field readable at trim, which a generated image neither satisfies nor can be checked for, and the menu has to be a true European page the printer accepts. EDITABILITY: the whole commission is defined by two people reprinting the menu every six weeks and rebuilding the deck for the next partner meeting with no designer, so a flat picture of a menu is worthless. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: does this frame have anything left in its highlights, does this record fit its frame at trim, did the list survive the import as two columns.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, the highlight and light-portion adjusters, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds and crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and detection_confidence are verified headless across 27 live calls; no upscaling is specced and the no-enlargement gate is checkable against the tradeoffs array. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt with its validator, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout and document_render_layout are verified fully headless and synchronous end to end, including per-row image binding through an @-prefixed CSV column plus additionalImageFiles, one record per page for PDF with page count equal to row count, per-record files in correct order via createSeparateFiles or a recordRange loop, and true 300 DPI raster. The truncation checkpoint rests on the verified facts that PDF-derived frame granularity is not under the agent's control and that no bleed can be introduced, so no bleed gate is asserted, and the reversed multi-record raster ordering trap is avoided by using only the PDF and createSeparateFiles routes. EXPRESS: a true 210 by 297 millimetre canvas at exactly 96 dpi, multi-page and mixed-canvas export in one call, and tables importing as real per-cell tables are verified, and column-count is a verified silent drop with the returned markup as the only channel and the rendition documented as page one only. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined photography passes the 70 KB threshold immediately. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit verified end to end, with the pairing refusal, non-standard numeric weights and all-or-nothing kit call all live findings. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, license returned a real 7360x4912 JPEG, boards cap at 12 placements per call with 201 meaning partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no variable QR, no fill_text, no animate_design, no replace_image, no download_design, no upscaling, no compositing, no OCR, no text-to-image, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no batch above 20.
